setting: You are all in Bristol, England, where you each live, and you belong to the same allotment society, so you know each other through committee work, the shared plot site and the odd work party.
openers: Post a photo of the leeks
Ask who can help at the next work party
Remind everyone about the tea urn rota
Send round the latest committee minutes
opener: Send round the latest committee minutes

Keith.knows: You know Tracy as the society secretary you work with on committee matters, Liam as the treasurer who keeps the accounts, Chloe as a plot holder whose plot is a few rows from yours, and Bethany as the newest member, who joined this year.
Keith.texts: You mostly message the group when there is society business to pass on, and now and then just to chat.
Keith.style: Very little emoji and no texting abbreviations.

Tracy.knows: You know Keith as the society chair you report to on committee matters, Liam as the treasurer you work alongside on the committee, Chloe as a plot holder you chat with on site, and Bethany as the new member you helped with her membership forms.
Tracy.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when something needs passing on from your secretary's role.
Tracy.style: A little emoji and few texting abbreviations.

Liam.knows: You know Keith as the society chair who sets the committee's direction, Tracy as the secretary who keeps the minutes and the paperwork, Chloe as a plot holder you see on work days, and Bethany as the new member you have spoken to about subscriptions.
Liam.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly about money or society payments, and not much otherwise.
Liam.style: Almost no emoji and no texting abbreviations.

Chloe.knows: You know Keith as the society chair who is friendly and always has an opinion on the plots, Tracy as the secretary who handles the forms, Liam as the treasurer who chases subs, and Bethany as the new member you have shown around the site.
Chloe.texts: You message the group fairly often, now and then starting chats about plot matters even when nobody has asked you anything.
Chloe.style: Quite a lot of emoji and some texting abbreviations.

Bethany.knows: You know Keith as the society chair who signed you up, Tracy as the secretary who sorted your forms, Liam as the treasurer who took your subscription, and Chloe as a plot holder who has been kind to you on site.
Bethany.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when you're checking something about your plot or your membership.
Bethany.style: Lots of emoji and plenty of texting abbreviations.

private_lines.Keith: You are retired after a long career as a civil engineer, and your days go to your own plot, walks around the city, and the society's committee work, with a steady routine at home in Bristol.
private_lines.Tracy: You work as an administrator at a secondary school in Bristol, which keeps you busy during the week, and you spend weekends on your plot and with friends, living in a busy household of your own routine.
private_lines.Liam: You lecture in finance at a university in Bristol, so your days go to teaching, marking and office hours, and your evenings and weekends go to your plot and home life in your own flat.
private_lines.Chloe: You work as a freelance graphic designer from a small home office in Bristol, so your days are set by client work and your own plot, and you live alone in a flat with your own routine.
private_lines.Bethany: You work part-time as a retail assistant in Bristol, so your days are split between shifts and your own time, and you share a flat with a few friends and keep a fairly loose routine.

text: [file: Committee minutes 19 Nov.pdf]
Item 4 is the subs chase. Liam has the figures.
Those are the final ones, I tidied the wording on item 6 about the gate key. Shout if anything looks wrong.
Item 4 is six outstanding as of Monday. I'll send names to Tracy so she can do the reminder letter.
Good. Put them on the board at the gate too.
hi is it me or do i still show as unpaid? i thought i did it in september
You're fine. Paid 14 Sept, it's on the sheet.
ok thanks, sorry
Is the tap by plot 40 fixed yet? Mine's been dripping for a fortnight and I'm not hauling water from the far end again
Not yet. Pete says Saturday, if he gets the washer from the merchant.
Saturday is what he said last week
Work party is still Saturday 10 till 1 btw, Keith has the list for the hedge. I can bring flasks
can I come? I'm off shift this weekend
Yes please! Bring gloves, the brambles are vicious
[photo: leeks in the cold frame]
they're doing better than I expected given the frost
They look well. You've got the spacing right.
🙏 I'm claiming it
Bank statement is in. Balance matches the sheet give or take the £12 I still need to check
Off the school run now. Is the committee meeting still 7 Dec or has it moved
7 Dec, 7pm, the church hall. Nothing has moved.
Ok good
Has anyone else had the bonfire leaflet through the gate? Looks like someone's tried to get the bins moved onto the path again
I saw it. Not the committee's doing. I'll raise it on the 7th if it comes up again.
Fair enough. Just didn't want it to be a surprise
£12 is a double entry for plot 22. Fixed. Sorry for the noise
anyone know if we need to bring our own tools saturday or does the society have some
Society has a few spades and a strimmer. Bring your own gloves and anything small you like to keep hold of
ok 👍 thanks Chloe
Ok, I'm off to bed. Work party is Saturday, Pete has the strimmer key.
Is it stupid that I've already started looking at seed catalogues
Ignore me, it's gone midnight
Pete has the washer. He'll be on plot 40 by nine on Saturday before we start.
Finally. Tell him thanks from me
Names for the reminder letter are on the sheet, tab 2. Same six as before.
Got them thanks. Letters going out after lunch
is 9 too early for the work party or is that when it starts
9 is when Pete opens the gate, 10 is when we actually start. Come early if you want a cup of tea first 🙂
ok ta
Two of the six have already replied saying they paid. Turns out one of them thought the letter was the bonfire leaflet 😬
Good. Ask them to forward the bank ref and I'll match it
[photo: seed catalogue, open at the runner beans]
don't judge
Runner beans are a lot of money for something you can buy in a supermarket
That's the point. I'm not buying them in a supermarket
Keith will say the Kelvedon ones are better
anyone still up
im up. cant sleep. nervous about the brambles lol
Gloves. Long sleeves. Tracy's flask is the good one, don't let anyone else take the mug
ok 👍
Flask is filled. Anyone bringing biscuits or is it just me doing the flapjack again
Biscuits are mine. I'll be at the gate for quarter to nine.
on my way. bus is late 😩
Just up. Pete has the washer in a bag like it's a prize
at the gate. is anyone else here yet or just me
Keith's here and I'm at the shed with the flask. Come on in Bethany, gloves are in the box by the water butt
found them ta
Tap on 40 is fixed. Pete says it was the washer and nothing else
Good. He's asked me to tell everyone to shut the gate properly, the fox was in again
🙏 finally
[photo: hedge before, brambles across the whole top section]
Bethany you're on the bramble end with Keith. Don't go near the nettles without a long sleeve
i have long sleeves. they are mostly long
Mostly is adequate. Pull the cut stuff onto the pile, not into the path.
Matched one of the two from yesterday. Other one still to check. Four still outstanding.
[photo: bramble haul, tarp, Keith looking pleased]
That is not a pleased face
it's the face you make when you're winning
i have a scratch on my wrist and i think i'm proud of it
Well done you. Plaster in the first aid tin by the gate
Ten minutes more and then we stop for the day. Flask is nearly done, Tracy
Flask is empty. The good mug is safe Chloe
thank you. I'll be checking
Pile is ready for Pete's van on Tuesday. Good work everyone
[photo: plot 40 tap running clear into a bucket]
Water. Cold. Nobody is more surprised than me
Glad the washer was worth the wait 😄
Clearing the last of the marking. Will look at the subs sheet tomorrow
legs hurt. worth it tho. chloe can i have seeds for the beans or is that a bad idea
Bethany they're in the shed in the tin marked BEANS. Take the Kelvedon ones, not the fancy ones
ok 👍
